children: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd (NSE:ADANIPORTS) reported rising Q2 and H1 profit, revenue and EBITDA, upgraded FY27 guidance and spent ₹10,521 crore on H1 capex as it won a 30-year Paradip concession, began Vizhinjam operations and drew a Motilal Oswal Buy with a ₹2,130 target.
Adani Ports Q2 Profit Up, Revenue, EBITDA Rise
: ADANIPORTS Q2: consolidated net profit rose, revenue and EBITDA increased, cargo volumes reported. H1 profit and revenue higher; management upgraded FY27 revenue, EBITDA and capex guidance.
: ADANIPORTS won a 30-year concession for Paradip Port CQ-I and CQ-II, adding 18 million tonnes of mechanized dry-bulk capacity, and began export–import operations at Vizhinjam port.
: Motilal Oswal reaffirms Buy on Adani Ports (ADANIPORTS) with INR 2,130 target, citing projected revenue, EBITDA and PAT growth to FY28, 17x FY28E EV/EBITDA and 17–21% CAGR.
Capex Spend Sharp At H1 FY27
: Adani Ports (ADANIPORTS) spent ₹10,521 crore on capex in H1 FY27, reflecting cash outlay for expansion and capital projects during the six-month period.
